newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian prince to parade in Rio carnival.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian prince to parade in Rio carnival.

text.p: Prince Joao de Orleans e Braganca, 42, the great-great-grandson of Portuguese King Joao VI who ruled Brazil in the last century, will bring a touch of royalty to this year's Rio de Janeiro carnival parades, samba school officials said on Tuesday.
A spokesman for the top Unidos da Tijuca samba school said the Brazilian prince had accepted the invitation to participate in their parade, which has Rio's botanical garden as its theme.
The botanical garden, believed to be the biggest tropical botanical park in the world, was founded in 1808 by King Joao VI.
Tijuca's eight carnival floats will recall the history of the garden and replicate the park's rich plant life from all over the world, the spokesman said.
Braganca had only one request for his taking part in the annual festivities. He ordered another 20 costumes so he could parade together with his friends.
